newsitem.title: UK: Britons object to ad violence after massacre.
newsitem.headline: Britons object to ad violence after massacre.

text.p: Viewer complaints about violence in advertisements have risen since a gunman shot 16 children and their teacher to death at a Scottish primary school in March, Britain's television regulatory agency said Tuesday.
The Independent Television Commission (ITC) said in its latest monthly report viewers had complained that two ads in particular were either violent or reminded them of violence.
One was for Skittles, a type of candy, that showed brightly dressed gangsters with stylised fruit heads "shooting" cartoon fruits at a group of children.
Some viewers said the ad reminded them of the massacre in the Scottish town of Dunblane.
The ITC said it decided not to uphold the August complaints, but had advised caution over showing weapons in advertisements.
An ITC spokeswoman said, "There is a greater sensitivity. ... You do not want to (do anything) that would bring back distressing memories."
The commission said it also decided not to uphold complaints about a different ad for Metz, a schnapps drink, that showed a male presenter wearing a ski mask.
Viewers said the image was disturbing because the man reminded them of a terrorist or rapist, but the ITC said that was not the intent of the advertiser.
The ITC also received complaints about ads viewers said were too sexually explicit.
It received 72 complaints about an ad for a headache remedy, Hedex Ibuprofen, that featured a couple who had sex after the woman's headache was cured.
